title: Is Courier HIPAA compliant? BAAs, SOC 2, and controls
summary: Yes. Courier has a HIPAA compliance program and signs BAAs on Enterprise. See its SOC 2 Type II controls, what the BAA covers, and what stays with you.
body_markdown:
Yes. Courier maintains a HIPAA compliance program and signs Business Associate Agreements (BAAs) with Enterprise customers. Its HIPAA report, SOC 2 Type II report, and penetration test results are in the[Courier Security Portal](https://security.courier.com/) . If you're building notifications for a healthcare product, here's what Courier runs on its side, the controls you get, and the parts that stay with you.


The short version: Courier handles the infrastructure, the audits, and the security monitoring. You decide what goes into each notification, and we recommend keeping protected health information (PHI) out of it. A notification that says "Your results are ready, sign in to view them" gets the patient to the details without carrying them.


## Courier's HIPAA compliance at a glance


Question Answer


Does Courier have a HIPAA compliance program? Yes. The HIPAA report is in the[Courier Security Portal](https://security.courier.com/) .


Does Courier sign a BAA? Yes, with Enterprise customers, as part of the Enterprise agreement.


What can the BAA cover? Every Courier service you use, including Journeys, Inbox, message logs, and AI features.


Does the BAA cover my SMS or email provider? You need to work with your email and SMS providers for their own HIPAA terms.


Is Courier audited? Yes. Courier holds a SOC 2 Type II report and runs an independent penetration test every year.


Can patient data stay in the EU? Yes. Send through the EU datacenter (Ireland), available on Business and Enterprise.


Can I self-host Courier? No. Courier is a managed cloud platform.


## What Courier runs


Area What Courier does


HIPAA program Maintains a HIPAA compliance program, documented in a HIPAA report.


SOC 2 Type II Holds a SOC 2 Type II report, an independent auditor's assessment of how Courier's security controls operate over time.


Other programs Maintains a PCI DSS program and supports your GDPR and CCPA obligations with a[Data Processing Addendum](https://www.courier.com/data-processing-addendum) .


Continuous monitoring Scans the full codebase continuously, scans every code change with frontier AI models tuned for security, monitors every open-source package it depends on, and runs AI scans of its code and network posture.


Infrastructure Runs on AWS across multiple availability zones, inside a private network with firewalls and intrusion detection.


Encryption Encrypts customer data at rest. The API accepts HTTPS only.


Staff access Staff use multi-factor authentication on internal systems, and access to customer data follows least privilege.


Testing An independent firm runs a penetration test every year.


Data location Your data stays in the[datacenter](https://www.courier.com/docs/security/data-residency) you send it through: US or EU (Ireland).


The monitoring runs between audits too, so security checks don't wait for the next SOC 2 report.[Security](https://www.courier.com/docs/security/overview) in the docs has the details.


## Controls you use


Courier gives you the controls a compliance review asks about:


- **Roles** limit what each teammate can change and how much of a message log they can see. Roles other than Administrator are on the Enterprise plan.
- **Configurable log retention** on the Enterprise plan lets you match message logs to your record-keeping policy.
- **Audit trail** on the Enterprise plan records API key rotations, role changes, publishes, and integration edits, with who and when.
- **Preferences** let patients choose which categories of notifications they get and on which channels. Opting out of a category applies on every channel.
- **Delivery logs** show what was sent, to whom, and how each provider responded, which is the evidence an audit asks for.
- **SSO and SCIM** keep workspace access tied to your identity provider. Teammates sign in through Google, GitHub, or Okta; Okta SSO and SCIM are on the Enterprise plan.
- **Scoped API keys** each cover one environment and one permission level, and **Inbox tokens** are minted by your backend per user, so the browser never holds your API key.


## AI features and PHI


Courier's AI features fit the same model. The Journeys AI node and AI Translation send data to OpenAI or Anthropic only when you use them, the providers don't store that data or train on it, and AI features can be included in your BAA. As with every notification, keep PHI out of prompts and template content.[AI features and your data](https://www.courier.com/docs/security/ai-and-your-data) lists exactly what each feature sends.


## What stays with you


HIPAA compliance is shared. These parts are yours:


- **What goes into each notification.** Send the alert, not the record. Keep diagnoses, results, and medication names behind sign-in in your own app. Push alerts show on lock screens and email subject lines show in inbox previews, so keep both generic.[HIPAA-compliant notifications](https://www.courier.com/blog/hipaa-compliant-notifications) walks through the pattern for SMS, push, email, and the inbox, and[appointment reminder templates](https://www.courier.com/blog/appointment-reminder-templates) has wording you can reuse.
- **Your delivery providers.** Courier sends through the SMS, email, and push providers you connect, and Courier's BAA covers Courier, not them. Review each provider's HIPAA terms.[Is Twilio HIPAA compliant?](https://www.courier.com/blog/is-twilio-hipaa-compliant) maps the common SMS providers, and[HIPAA-compliant email](https://www.courier.com/blog/hipaa-compliant-email) covers email.
- **Consent and registration for texts.** The TCPA and A2P 10DLC apply even when a text carries no PHI.[Is texting patients a HIPAA violation?](https://www.courier.com/blog/is-texting-patients-a-hipaa-violation) covers both, and[A2P 10DLC registration](https://www.courier.com/blog/a2p-10dlc-registration) walks through registering.

## Getting a BAA


Courier signs BAAs with Enterprise customers. The BAA is part of your Enterprise agreement, and its scope is set during contracting and can cover every Courier service you use. We work through it with you one-on-one, along with any other security review questions you have.


To start,[talk to our team](https://www.courier.com/request-demo) . For how Courier supports healthcare teams, see[Courier for healthcare](https://www.courier.com/solutions/healthcare) , and for BAAs and log retention, see[HIPAA compliance and BAAs](https://www.courier.com/docs/security/hipaa) in the docs.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is Courier HIPAA compliant?


Yes. Courier maintains a HIPAA compliance program, documented in a HIPAA report in the Courier Security Portal, and signs BAAs with Enterprise customers. Compliance is shared: Courier runs the platform and its security controls, and you decide what goes into each notification.


### Does Courier sign a BAA?


Courier signs BAAs with Enterprise customers. The BAA is part of the Enterprise agreement, and its scope can cover every Courier service you use, including Journeys, Inbox, message logs, and AI features.


### Does Courier's BAA cover my SMS or email provider?


Courier's BAA covers Courier. Your SMS, email, and push providers deliver the messages, so you need to work with them for their own HIPAA terms.


### Is Courier HIPAA certified?


HIPAA has no official certification for vendors. Courier maintains a HIPAA compliance program, documented in its HIPAA report, and holds a SOC 2 Type II report. Both are in the Courier Security Portal.


### Is Courier SOC 2 compliant?


Courier holds a SOC 2 Type II report from an independent auditor. Request access to it in the Courier Security Portal.


### Can I send PHI through Courier?


Courier recommends keeping PHI out of notification content and the data you send. A notification that tells the patient something is ready, and links to the details behind sign-in, works on every channel without carrying PHI.


### Can I send appointment reminders and lab result alerts through Courier?


Yes. Courier sends appointment reminders and "new results are ready" alerts across SMS, email, push, and in-app, with channel fallback and patient preferences built in. Keep clinical details out of the message and link to your app for the rest.


### Does Courier use my data to train AI models?


No. Courier's AI providers, OpenAI and Anthropic, don't store the data Courier's AI features send them or use it to train models, and AI features run only when you use them.


### Can Courier keep patient data in the EU?


Yes. Courier runs separate US and EU (Ireland) datacenters with no data shared between them. Send EU patients' notifications through the EU datacenter, available on Business and Enterprise.


### Where do I get Courier's security reports?


Courier's HIPAA report, SOC 2 Type II report, and penetration test results are in the[Courier Security Portal](https://security.courier.com/) . For more detail during a security review, contact Courier.
